'''History of Star Wars CCG''' is a timeline of the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG), from Decipher's first release in 1995 through the volunteer [[Players Committee]] era. Detail lives on the linked pages.

== Decipher era (1995–2001) ==

Decipher, Inc. of Norfolk, Virginia, published SWCCG under a Lucasfilm license. [[Premiere Limited]] shipped in December 1995 and [[Theed Palace]] (12 December 2001) was the last Decipher expansion.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> In 1998 Lucasfilm renewed the license to cover ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="wp" /> Decipher also published [[Young Jedi]], a separate ''Phantom Menace'' card game, from May 1999 to September 2001.<ref name="yjcl">[http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Young Jedi Card Lists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021201080954/http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> From November 2001 it also published [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]] (2001–2007).<ref name="lotrpc">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008212029/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher also published two other ''Star Wars'' card games, [[Young Jedi]] and the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref>Lee Bates, [http://www.scifi.com/sfw/issue199/games.html Jedi Knights Trading Card Game (review)], ''Science Fiction Weekly'', SciFi.com (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20071211183732/http://www.scifi.com/sfw/issue199/games.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Loss of the license (2001) ==

''See also: [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]] and [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]]''

In July 2000 Decipher presented marketing, digital and second-edition proposals to Lucasfilm executives.<ref name="pres2000">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020602000629/http://decipher.com/starwars/presentationexcerpts.html Excerpts from Decipher's July 2000 Presentation to Lucasfilm], decipher.com (Internet Archive, 2 June 2002)</ref> Lucasfilm did not extend the license. Decipher announced the end on 28 December 2001, and the trading-card rights went to Wizards of the Coast.<ref name="ann">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (Internet Archive, 1 June 2002)</ref><ref name="tfn2001">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Lucasfilm_terminates_Deciphers_Star_Wars_License_69604.asp Lucasfilm terminates Decipher's Star Wars License], TheForce.Net (28 December 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010072854/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Lucasfilm_terminates_Deciphers_Star_Wars_License_69604.asp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="icv2">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Wizards of the Coast Gets Star Wars CCG], ICv2 (1 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008201620/https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Internet Archive]</ref> Wizards published its own, incompatible [[Star Wars Trading Card Game]] (2002–2005).<ref name="icv2" /> Full account: [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]]. Decipher's later years: [[Decipher after the Star Wars license|Decipher after the license]].

Third-party repacks of Decipher packs sold after the license ended are on [[Unofficial repackaged products]]. The secondary market for Decipher-era singles and sealed product is covered in [[Aftermarket and collecting]].

== Players Committee formation (2002) ==

On 25 January 2002 Warren Holland announced the first Star Wars Player Advocates, a volunteer Players' Committee to carry on tournaments, rulings and player support.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Internet Archive, 11 June 2002)</ref> The committee works with the cooperation of Decipher and Lucasfilm and distributes Virtual cards electronically only.<ref name="pcabout">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about-us/ About Us], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250316172158/https://www.starwarsccg.org/about-us/ Internet Archive]</ref> DeckTech held a second FreedomCon in Lansdale, Pennsylvania, in October 2002.<ref name="fc2-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon Philadelphia 2002 home page], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030112115941/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 12 January 2003]</ref> See [[History of the Players Committee]], [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] and [[Players Committee advocates]].

== Virtual Original (2002–2009) ==

The first Virtual Card Set was announced on 12 February 2002 and became tournament-legal on 9 March 2002: twelve printable (V) slips sleeved over Premiere cards.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net (12 February 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008194445/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Internet Archive)</ref> Numbered Virtual Sets followed, from [[Virtual Set 1: Legacy]] to [[Virtual Set 17: The Force Unleashed]]. The PC ran Worlds from [[2002 World Championship|2002]] on. See [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]], [[Cancelled Virtual Sets]] and [[List of SWCCG tournaments]].

== Virtual Legacy blocks (2009–2014) ==

In 2009 the PC regrouped the previous 18 Virtual Sets into six thematic Virtual Blocks.<ref name="vb1">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf] ("Official text as of 7 December 2009"), res.starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195542/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> Blocks 7–9 followed, and Virtual Block 9.1 shipped on 10 January 2014.<ref name="vb91">[https://web.archive.org/web/20140115143606/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/v-set-9-1-is-live/ V-Set 9.1 is Live], starwarsccg.org (Internet Archive, 15 January 2014)</ref> See [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]], [[Virtual Legacy]], [[Virtual Block 1]] to [[Virtual Block 9]] and [[Virtual Shields]].

== Reset to the present (2014–) ==

On 25 July 2014 the Advocate Council announced a reset of the Standard format to a small base set of Virtual cards. All pre-Reset Virtual cards moved to a new Legacy format.<ref name="reset">[http://web.archive.org/web/20141020142523id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/reset-of-standard-format/ Reset of Standard Format], starwarsccg.org (25 July 2014; Internet Archive)</ref> [[Virtual Set 0]] and the Virtual Set 1 preview were posted on 25 September 2014 and were legal immediately.<ref name="resetpdf">[http://web.archive.org/web/20141009180356id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/pdf-of-reset-list-posted-virtual-set-0-and-virtual-set-1-preview/ PDF of Reset List Posted – Virtual Set 0 and Virtual Set 1 Preview], starwarsccg.org (25 September 2014; Internet Archive)</ref> See [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]].

Current Virtual sets have continued since, from [[Virtual Set 1]] to [[Virtual Set 27]].<ref name="slips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240920164229/https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Internet Archive]</ref> Online play runs on [[GEMP]]. Yearly Worlds hubs run from [[2014 World Championship]] onward; see [[Championships]] and [[List of SWCCG tournaments]].
